findings.summary: Payload lifetime is now correctly tied to the child (onExit on exit/error), which fixes the prior blocker. Side effect worth recording: on the normal long-running path spawnWorkerProcess settles on the SPAWN_READY_GRACE_MS timer and marks itself settled, so the later exit handler short-circuits and onExit never runs — the a8d-worker-input-*.json file stays in tmpdir for the process lifetime. This is the safe direction (worker can always read --input) and the spec imposes no cleanup requirement, but the code comment reads as if cleanup always happens.

AgentRunUnresolvedError is now rethrown out of runWrite and surfaces on the CLI as stderr naming agent-run plus exit 2, satisfying spec §1.4/P8/P9. It is raised after the open→in_flight CAS has already been published, so a misconfigured deployment leaves one card in_flight per failed tick (reclaimed to open on the next tick). Resolving agent-run before the first irreversible write would make the failure fail-fast with zero bus writes; the spec does not require it.

Mutation self-check §4 was executed for W1/W2/W4/W6 with per-assertion attribution and verified-clean restores; W3 and W5 are argued rather than run (dev-note states P4's adjacent-pair assertion and P8/P9 respectively would catch them). The argument holds against the committed tests (P4 asserts indexOf('--input') >= 0; P9 asserts runChannelWrite rejects with AgentRunUnresolvedError), and the gap is disclosed rather than hidden.
